finding.claim: The /mirror endpoint fetches a user-supplied URL after a flawed host check. The check uses endswith("example.com") with no leading dot, so it also accepts hosts such as attackerexample.com or evilexample.com. ALLOWED_SUFFIX (".example.com") is defined but never used. The scheme and port are not restricted, and the resolved IP is not checked. An attacker can register a lookalike domain and point it at internal or metadata addresses such as 169.254.169.254 or 127.0.0.1. They can also use userinfo-style URLs such as http://x@evilexample.com. The server then makes the request and returns the response length.

trace.note: url taken from the query string
weak check: host.endswith("example.com"), no dot boundary

finding.guards_checked: Only the endswith("example.com") hostname check at line 13. There is no dot boundary, scheme allowlist, port restriction, or DNS/IP resolution check. httpx does not follow redirects by default, so redirect-based bypass is not a factor. The response body is not returned, only its length, which limits the impact to blind SSRF plus a size oracle. The /ping endpoint uses a hardcoded URL and is not vulnerable.

verdict.guard_found: Only host.endswith("example.com") at mirror.py:13 (suffix check, no dot boundary); ALLOWED_SUFFIX at line 7 is unused; no scheme, port, or IP checks, and no auth or middleware.
verdict.reason: The `url` query parameter (mirror.py:11) is attacker-controlled and reaches `c.get(url)` (mirror.py:16) guarded only by the bypassable `endswith("example.com")` check at mirror.py:13, so lookalike hosts such as evilexample.com pass.
